Per-file terminal-state fixes preserve the consumed additive result contract; the CLI migration preserves all toolkit commands and flags. Viewer, VS Code, configuration documentation, comment cleanup, gitignore, and rules-integrity tests require no toolkit adaptation. Built-in rules and the file allowlist are unchanged.

Compatible after review in issue #52 and workflow run 30807718526. The expanded default allowlist intentionally excludes snapshots, fixtures, testdata, and generated files from the effective review scope; session-comment CLI, truncated-chat retry, and test refactoring require no toolkit adaptation. The consumed Go MCP SDK remains v1.6.1.

Compatible after review in issue #60, workflow run 30987719228, and checksum-verified local probes. The upstream GitLab fail-open example, resumable full scan, model catalog, CLI validation, documentation, and CI changes do not alter consumed toolkit behavior.

Compatible after adjacent review against 1.8.7 plus workflow and checksum-verified local probes. Nix and Haskell allowlist and built-in rule support extend OCR's effective review-scope/rules contract and are accepted without toolkit adaptation or completion of BL-008/BL-009/BL-010. Viewer, VS Code, test, and CI changes are outside the consumed toolkit contract; the Go MCP SDK remains v1.6.1.

Reviewed viewer, benchmark, plugin, Pages, code_search, documentation, SPDX, and CI changes. Native code_search option-like reference hardening improves upstream security; toolkit CLI, result, MCP, and configuration contracts remain compatible.

Reviewed viewer, CLI, internal timeout, deterministic tool-parameter rendering, documentation, test, CI, and dependency changes. Valid toolkit invocations remain compatible; deterministic rendering improves reproducibility without completing toolkit profiles or telemetry.

Compatible after human review in issue #73 and workflow run 31465539451. JSON preview now honors --format json without creating a session store; additive comment thinking is preserved by OCR but remains private because toolkit posting does not render it. Nim built-in rules and .nim/.nims/.nimble allowlist entries extend the effective rules contract. Merge-base documentation confirms the toolkit range model. Per-file limits and retry codes are upstream configuration capabilities, while Mistral/MiniMax providers, QCA, upstream GitLab example, Pages/viewer, installation, scan documentation, and other documentation/CI changes are not toolkit-owned contracts. The Go MCP SDK remains v1.6.1.

Compatible after adjacent qualification in issue #72 and workflow run 31465539451. Viewer filtering/layout, CodeQL workflow permissions, upstream agent/retry documentation, and Anthropic cache-breakpoint optimization do not change toolkit-owned CLI, result, posting, configuration, or MCP contracts. JSON preview, full review, additive thinking, and toolkit result/posting consumer probes pass; the Go MCP SDK remains v1.6.1.

Compatible after human adjacent source review in issue #78 and hosted workflow run 31571999318. The release tags diverge only because the retry documentation commit was reapplied with the same stable patch-id; no 1.9.1 runtime behavior is lost. OCR directory-only gitignore matching now follows ancestor, glob, and root-anchor semantics and compatibly improves the toolkit-consumed review-selection boundary. New built-in providers, Pages/viewer, Action pinning, skill/retry/agent documentation, and upstream CI changes require no toolkit adaptation. CLI, preview, result/posting, rules/allowlist, and MCP contracts remain compatible; the Go MCP SDK remains v1.6.1.

Compatible after human adjacent source review in issue #82 and hosted workflow run 31778152040. Required review flags, JSON result and manifest, structured comment metadata, rules/allowlist, and the Go MCP SDK v1.6.1 remain compatible. Optional retry_report is additive observability and remains private; SARIF, no-review, trusted resume lineage, session affinity, stabilized upstream item fingerprints, and argument diagnostics require no toolkit runtime adaptation. Case-insensitive user filters improve selection without changing built-in allowlist membership. The grace round can add ordinary findings without changing consumed outcome semantics. GitHub Shields badges are presentation-only; the toolkit independently projects only normalized metadata at its GitLab rendering boundary.

Compatible after human adjacent source review in issue #90 and hosted workflow run 31868292800. Required review flags, JSON preview/result and manifest, structured comment metadata, rules/allowlist, and the Go MCP SDK v1.6.1 remain compatible. The new terminal-only session line is not emitted for JSON output and therefore does not alter toolkit result parsing, stderr diagnostics, or posting. TraceSummary is an internal upstream refactor with exact-output tests and no consumed API change. The session identifier is useful correlation evidence for BL-017, but it remains OCR-owned, high-cardinality run identity rather than a reason to add a duplicate toolkit telemetry layer. Provider presets/base URLs, resume/opencode behavior, Pages/install/docs/CI changes, and upstream tests require no toolkit adaptation.

Compatible after human adjacent source review in issue #93 and hosted workflow run 32000131436, plus a checksum-verified local Darwin arm64 qualification. Required review flags now explicitly include --max-tokens-budget; real OCR preserves completed findings and emits a partial manifest with budget-attributed failed coverage when that cap stops dispatch. The new scan budget summary is scan-only and does not expand the toolkit review boundary. Swift built-in rules and default test exclusions change the effective recommended-OCR rules contract. Cross-file relocation and the conservative tool-based review filter improve upstream finding positioning/filtering without changing toolkit result, MCP, posting, or authority contracts. The kimi-global preset, plugin marketplaces, viewer handling, and documentation require no toolkit adaptation.

Compatible after human adjacent review in issue #105 and hosted workflow run 32144971874. Required review flags, JSON preview/result and manifest, structured comment metadata, partial budget behavior, target-rule selection, and optional provider/model capabilities remain compatible. Notebook, R, Zig, Elm, Jsonnet, Thrift, Cap’n Proto, properties, PO, and POT support extends the effective recommended-OCR rules/allowlist contract and requires a Rules changelog entry but no toolkit runtime adaptation. api_key_cmd/auth_token_cmd is an upstream operator configuration and shell-execution boundary; the toolkit neither configures nor invokes it, keeps OCR_LLM_TOKEN environment-backed, and does not adopt a second credential-command interface. Updater, CI, license, Pages, localization, and documentation changes require no toolkit adaptation.

Compatible after reviewed adjacent source and release comparison plus hosted checksum-verified Linux probes. Gemini provider and mirror-aware installers are additive operator/upstream boundaries; the Go MCP, review flags, result/manifest, target-rule, budget, and session contracts consumed by the toolkit remain compatible. No toolkit CI adaptation is required beyond version and checksum pins.

Compatible after reviewed adjacent source and release comparison, hosted checksum-verified Linux probes, and checksum-verified Darwin arm64 local probes. Bedrock/SigV4 configuration is an additive upstream provider boundary not configured by the toolkit. Native severity is confined to upstream skill instructions; OCR result severity/category fields already match the tolerant toolkit contract. JSON/SARIF progress moves to stderr for human audience, while the toolkit uses agent audience and consumes the unchanged JSON result. Review flags, manifest, target-rule, budget, MCP multi-tool composition, and session contracts remain compatible. No toolkit CI adaptation is required beyond version and checksum pins.

Compatible after hosted checksum-verified Linux qualification, reviewed adjacent upstream source, and checksum-verified Darwin arm64 qualification evidence. OCR 1.9.9 makes background-file take precedence over inline background, so the toolkit now rejects both caller background inputs and remains the sole background-file owner. Distinct static main-loop stop reasons remain within the existing failed-item reason contract and are covered through result retention, publication projection, DLP, and posting diagnostics. Provider tool-choice test expansion does not change a consumed wire contract.

Compatible after checksum-verified hosted Linux qualification and direct adjacent source review. OCR 1.9.10 changes terminal retry-report grouping only; structured ocr.llm-retry-report/v1, result, manifest, and toolkit review semantics remain unchanged and private. Background wait and safe resume checkpoint fixes apply to ocr scan, while the toolkit invokes ocr review. VS Code merge-file enumeration is outside the toolkit contract. No telemetry, receipt, DLP, severity, outcome, or approval input changes.

Reviewed OCR 1.9.10...1.10.0 source, hosted Linux wire evidence, and exact Darwin numeric-boundary evidence: semantic grouping, path-aware comments, default medium two-round review, private additive group metadata, output-file capability, git diagnostics, the 16384 completion cap, and template-owned max-tools behavior are compatible with toolkit boundaries; toolkit retains exclusive result-path ownership, explicit 4096 cap support, and closed normalization projection.

Compatible after semantic review for #146. The toolkit consumes bounded private session cache keys and .m language resolution with MATLAB and Objective-C rules. Result and manifest contracts, inherited completion cap 16384, explicit cap 4096, medium effort, and max-tools semantics remain unchanged. The upstream GitHub Action, delegate skill, npm launcher, built-in provider preset, and repository-local providers.go rule are not consumed because the toolkit uses the native binary with explicit protocol and configuration.

Compatible after human review in issue #151 and hosted workflow run 33055459209. OCR 1.10.2 adds tracked grouping and grace-round requests, aligns grouping with the inherited 16384 completion cap, and adds Solidity/Vyper review rules without changing toolkit result, manifest, medium-effort, max-tools, DLP, receipt, telemetry, or approval contracts. Session comparison and reusable GitHub Action checkpoint ranges are not consumed; the latter only partially overlaps BL-021. The original machine automatic-safe classification was overridden because feature-bearing release notes require human review.

Compatible after hosted checksum-verified Linux qualification in run 33158664020 and direct adjacent source review in issue #155. OCR 1.11.0 changes grouping and other-file inventory to status-first entries with churn, preserves provider-native reasoning across assistant turns, removes the filter's forced tool choice, scales subtask timeout by review rounds, improves file_find subpaths, and adds Handlebars/Mustache rules. The toolkit qualification harness consumes the inventory shape and runtime-facing boundaries while provider reasoning and native payloads remain private and unconsumed. Result/manifest schemas, inherited 16384 completion cap, operator-selected positive override support, medium effort, max-tools, receipt v5, DLP, telemetry, and approval contracts remain unchanged; the toolkit leaves the override unset and recommends no provider-specific value. Upstream action, plugin, launcher, locale, provider preset, and config-command validation changes are not consumed.
